newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Energy says NZ gas well meeting expectations.
newsitem.headline: FCL Energy says NZ gas well meeting expectations.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy said on Thursday that drilling of its onshore Mangahewa-2 well east of New Plymouth in New Zealand's North Island was ahead of schedule and meeting expectations.
The well is being drilled to test the potential for "tight gas production" from the Mangahewa formation. It was spudded on December 15 and as at January 22 had reached a depth of 3,733 metres.

"The well is five days ahead of schedule and has met all of Fletcher Challenge Energy's expectations in terms of geological formations and the depths at which they are being encountered. Gas shows and reservoir quality are also in line with expectations," the company said.

The primary target reservoir sandstones, the Mangahewa formation of the Eocene age, had been entered and a core sample taken. Drilling would continue into the secondary Omata shales and Kaimiro formations which are expected to be encountered at 4,350 and 4,500 metres respectively.

"Gas has been encountered in the primary target reservoir and it is planned that selected sandstone intervals in the Mangahewa formation will be stimulated by large scale hydraulic fracturing.
